items.title: Ask, Condition or Abstain: Reinforcement Learning for Missing-Premise Reasoning
items.summary_1line: Answer-only reinforcement learning (RL) trains reasoning models to solve fully specified problems, but many realistic queries omit a premise needed for a unique answer. In this setting, the useful response is not alwa...
items.editor_note: New arXiv paper training reasoning models to ask, condition, or abstain instead of guessing when a query is missing a necessary premise, closing a known gap in answer-only RL.

editorial.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose weekly grouping of unrelated RL items, not a developing story. Recent entries range from Moonshot AI's open-sourced AgentENV framework for scaling agentic RL training to a paper modeling clinical-residency training as an RL problem.
editorial.whats_new: A new arXiv paper trains reasoning models to ask, condition on an assumption, or abstain when a query is missing a premise needed for a unique answer — a gap in standard answer-only RL training.
editorial.why_it_matters: Answer-only RL, the default for most reasoning-model fine-tuning, never teaches a model to flag an underspecified request; that's a real failure mode for agents built to act on ambiguous user or tool input.
editorial.take_for_builders: RL-fine-tuning a reasoning or tool-calling model? Check whether your reward function penalizes abstaining or asking on underspecified input — answer-only RL trains models to guess rather than flag a missing premise.

beats.headline: Moonshot AI and kvcache-ai open-source AgentENV to scale agentic RL
beats.summary: New open-source framework targets scaling agentic reinforcement learning training — a shipped tool, not an academic result like the papers alongside it.

beats.headline: ResidencyRL simulates clinical-residency training as an RL problem
beats.summary: New arXiv work models how physicians convert academic knowledge into clinical judgment through simulated patient encounters with staged feedback, mirroring real residency training.

beats.headline: New paper trains RL reasoning models to ask, condition, or abstain on missing-premise queries
beats.summary: Targets a known failure mode of answer-only RL: forcing a unique answer even when the query omits a premise needed to produce one.

open_questions: Does AgentENV's scaling approach hold up against existing agentic-RL training frameworks, or is it mainly a Moonshot-internal tool going public?
Does ResidencyRL's simulated training transfer to real clinical decision-making, or only to the benchmark's synthetic cases?
Does the ask/condition/abstain method generalize beyond its evaluated missing-premise benchmarks to real-world ambiguous tool-calling prompts?
